draft.title: Purposes of punishment
card: discouraging crime through fear of punishment. Specific deterrence aims at the offender. General deterrence aims at others who might offend.
making the offender pay for the wrong done. The punishment should match the seriousness of the crime.
helping the offender change, for example through treatment or training, so they do not reoffend.
removing the offender's ability to offend again, for example by keeping them in prison. Denunciation is the court publicly stating that the conduct is wrong.
draft.remember: A sentence can serve several purposes, and a judge weighs them against each other.

a.q: A judge gives an offender a sentence mainly to help them change through a drug treatment program. Which purpose is this?
a.why: Treatment aims to change the offender so they do not reoffend, which is rehabilitation. Incapacitation is the tempting wrong answer, but it is about preventing offending by removing the ability to offend, not by changing the person.
a.clue: Which purpose is about changing the offender?

b.q: A judge says a long prison term for a fraudster will warn other people tempted to commit similar frauds. Which purpose is the judge relying on?
b.why: The warning is aimed at other people who might offend, which is general deterrence. Specific deterrence is the tempting wrong answer, because it aims at discouraging this offender, not the wider public.
b.clue: Who is the warning meant for: the offender or others?

problems.detail: Denunciation is put inside the incapacitation bullet without its own heading. Students could read it as part of incapacitation rather than a separate purpose of punishment.

proposal.title: Purposes of punishment
card: Deterrence discourages crime through fear of punishment. Specific deterrence aims at the offender, and general deterrence aims at others who might offend.
Retribution makes the offender pay for the wrong, in proportion to how serious the crime was. Denunciation is the court publicly stating that the conduct is wrong.
Rehabilitation helps the offender change, for example through treatment or training, so they do not reoffend. Incapacitation removes their ability to offend, for example by keeping them in prison.
A sentence can serve several of these purposes at once, and they can pull against each other. The judge weighs them to reach a fitting sentence.
proposal.remember: Judges balance five aims: deter, punish, denounce, reform and incapacitate.
